verifications.notes: Date 2017 and causal arrow to 2023 agents check out, and Q2/Q3 hold: post-2017 frontier models are overwhelmingly Transformer-based. Q1 is overstated, however: RNN/LSTM systems (GNMT) already did production translation and parallel convolutional rivals (ByteNet 2016, ConvS2S 2017) were concurrent, so the Transformer was a large efficiency/quality improvement, not the removal of an impossibility; Q2 independently carries the gate.

Date 1945 (First Draft on EDVAC) is correct and strictly before the parent, and Q2/Q3 hold for mainstream computing. Weakness is priority/authorship: Eckert (Jan 1944 memo) and Mauchly had the design before von Neumann, Turing's 1936 universal machine and Zuse's 1936 patents anticipated stored instructions, so sole attribution to the 1945 report is disputed; also ENIAC was already general-purpose, making Q1 an impracticality claim rather than impossibility.

Q2/Q3 hold: cross-entropy is in fact the GPT-class pre-training objective. Weakness is dating/naming: Shannon 1948 introduced entropy (and a relative-entropy quantity), but 'cross-entropy' as a named two-distribution loss and training objective crystallized later (Kullback-Leibler 1951 and after), and the evaluator's own Q1 was only partial, so the 1948 label is anachronistic though the underlying quantity is present.

Date 2013 correct and Q2 holds (wide transfer and adoption). Weaknesses: Q1 and Q3 were only partial in evaluation, embeddings already existed via Bengio 2003, and GloVe (2014) was a near-simultaneous substitute reaching comparable vectors from co-occurrence counts, so necessity attaches to scalable embeddings generally, not word2vec uniquely; its line to Transformers is also indirect since Transformers learn their own embeddings.

Date 2007 (CUDA 1.0, Feb 2007) correct and Q2/Q3 hold for frontier training on NVIDIA/CUDA. Q1 is overstated: GPGPU was already possible via shader hacks and BrookGPU (2004, by CUDA lead Ian Buck), and AMD's Close-to-Metal/Stream (2006) was a concurrent alternative platform, so CUDA removed impracticality rather than impossibility and the time was partly ripe.

Cauchy 1847 date is correct and Q2 holds: gradient methods do train essentially all neural networks. Weakness: independent rediscovery/formalization followed (Hadamard 1907, Curry 1944, Robbins-Monro stochastic approximation 1951), and Newton's method and least squares predated it, so Q3 necessity for this specific 1847 formulation is downgraded; the evaluator already scored Q3 only partial.

Date 1970 and the Q3 efficiency claim hold: reverse mode is asymptotically the tractable exact-gradient method for scalar-loss, many-parameter models, and Q1/Q2 pass mathematically. Weakness is paternity/causality: the Finnish thesis had no traceable influence on AI's adoption of backpropagation, which was independently re-derived by Werbos (1974) and Rumelhart et al. (1986), so Linnainmaa has priority but the transmission line to the parent is via reinvention.

Verified once across both edges (to the 2023 agent and to the 2017 Transformer). arXiv Sept 2014 date is correct (ICLR 2015) and Q2 holds: the Transformer directly generalizes this soft alignment to self-attention. Weakness: attention was concurrent, not solitary - Graves et al.'s Neural Turing Machine (2014) used content-based attention and Luong et al. (2015) supplied rival scoring forms - and Q1 shows long-sentence degradation relieved, i.e. improvement over a working fixed-vector baseline, not impossibility removed.

Date Dec 2015 correct and before the 2017 Transformer, whose blocks do reuse identity shortcuts, so Q2 carries the gate. Clear multiple against Q3: Highway Networks (Srivastava, Greff & Schmidhuber, May 2015) trained very deep feedforward nets with gated skip connections seven months earlier and ResNet is its open-gate variant, a fact the ResNet paper acknowledges as concurrent work; Q1 was also only partial.

Date 1986 correct as the popularizing Rumelhart-Hinton-Williams paper and Q2 holds, but this is a textbook multiple/priority case: reverse-mode AD was published by Linnainmaa (1970), applied to networks by Werbos (1974/1982), and independently published by Parker and LeCun (1985). The 1986 node is a rediscovery and popularization, so necessity is 'the time was ripe', not sole invention.

Date 2014 correct and Q2 holds: the Transformer inherited the encoder-decoder transduction framing. Clear multiple: Cho et al. (2014) independently proposed the RNN encoder-decoder the same year (EMNLP 2014), with Sutskever et al. adding deep LSTMs and input reversal, so seq2seq was a simultaneous invention; Q1 and Q3 were only partial in evaluation.

Date 2016 correct and before the 2017 Transformer, which does embed LayerNorm in every sub-layer, so Q2 as stated passes. Weakness: Q1/Q3 were only partial and ready substitutes exist - BatchNorm (2015) preceded it and RMSNorm (2019) has since replaced LayerNorm in many frontier LLMs (e.g. LLaMA), showing this specific normalization is replaceable rather than necessary.

Attacks fail: 2003 date is correct, no simultaneous rival neural language model jointly learning distributed word representations was found (earlier distributed representations were not a trained neural LM, and word2vec/GloVe came a decade later), and the causal line into embedding-based NLP and the Transformer's learned token embeddings is documented. Q1 was only partial, but Q2 independently and cleanly carries the gate.

1614 publication date correct and Q2 holds (log-probability additivity underlies entropy/cross-entropy). Classic multiple against Q3: Jost Burgi independently invented logarithms (conceived c.1588, tables published 1620), as Britannica and MacTutor confirm, so logarithms were a parallel discovery and the time was ripe; Napier retains publication priority only.

Q2 holds: the 1877 paper did establish entropy as proportional to the logarithm of a probability, the move Shannon generalized. Weakness is attribution of the formula itself: Boltzmann never wrote S = k log W or introduced the constant k - Planck wrote that form c.1900-01 and named it for him - so the node's named equation is anachronistic even though the 1877 conceptual contribution and date are real.

Q1's identity (maximizing log-likelihood = minimizing cross-entropy under the empirical distribution) is mathematically sound and Q2 holds. Weakness: maximum likelihood had extensive pre-Fisher use by Lagrange, Laplace, Gauss, Thiele and Edgeworth, and Fisher's own work spans 1912-1922, so 1922 is systematization/naming rather than invention; also the equivalence to cross-entropy is retrospective, not a documented influence on Shannon 1948.

Attacks fail: the 1902 text does state entropy as -k sum p_i log p_i over an arbitrary ensemble distribution, no earlier general form was found (Boltzmann covers only the equiprobable special case, which Gibbs reduces to), the date is strictly before 1948, and Shannon's entropy is formally this quantity. The Boltzmann-versus-Gibbs contrast strengthens rather than undermines Q3.

Date 1928 correct, Shannon explicitly builds on Hartley, and Q2 holds, so the node survives. Weakness: Hartley's H = n log s covers only equiprobable symbols and rests on Nyquist's related 1924/1928 telegraph-transmission work, and the step that actually yields entropy/cross-entropy for arbitrary distributions is Shannon's 1948 generalization, making Hartley a genuine but partial precursor rather than the full measure.

Q2 holds definitionally: cross-entropy is E_p[-log q] and Huygens 1657 is the first published treatise systematizing expectation. Weakness against Q3's 'no substitute in 1657': Pascal and Fermat had already explicitly calculated mathematical expectation in their 1654 correspondence (which Huygens learned of in Paris in 1655 and himself disclaimed priority for), so Huygens is first publisher/systematizer, not sole inventor.
